name: Dubuk
instructions: 1. Soak Gahat dal overnight and grind it into a coarse, thick paste using minimal water.
2. Heat mustard oil in an iron kadhai until it reaches a smoking point.
3. Add cumin seeds and a pinch of asafoetida to the oil.
5. Add the ground dal paste to the kadhai and roast it well on low heat until it turns golden brown and aromatic.
6. Add turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt, mixing thoroughly.
7. Gradually add warm water while stirring continuously to prevent lumps, adjusting to a thick soup-like consistency.
8. Cover and simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
9. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with steamed rice or mandua (finger millet) roti.
description: Dubuk is a protein-rich, winter specialty from the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand. Traditionally prepared in cast-iron vessels, it is a staple comfort food known for its earthy, nutty flavor and medicinal properties, often served as a nutritious meal for mountain dwellers.
